newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Executions of Uighurs will spark more riots-exiles.
newsitem.headline: Executions of Uighurs will spark more riots-exiles.

text.p: The Chinese authorities' execution of ethnic Uighurs for their role in bloody riots in the Moslem region of Xinjiang in February will stir up new protests, an exiled Uighur organisation said on Saturday.

"These actions (by Chinese authorities) will lead to new spontaneous and massive protest actions," Modan Mukhlisi, representative of the United Revolutionary Front of Eastern Turkestan, told Reuters in the Kazakh capital. "The authorities are merely pushing Uighurs to active revolt."

Chinese television said on Saturday that three men had been sentenced to death on Thursday and 27 to prison terms for crimes of malicious wounding, arson and hooliganism during the riots in Yining near the Kazakh border that killed at least nine people and injured 198.
A local media official said the executions had been carried out on the same day as the sentencing by the Yili District Intermediate Court.

Mukhlisi said the real number of those sentenced to death was seven, and that the trial and executions took place in Yining. "This was a show trial, and before their death the seven were exposed in a truck to the whole town," he said, adding that local authorities had imposed a curfew after the trial.
Xinjiang, a vast region that is home to the Uighurs and many other Turkic-speaking peoples, has a long history of ethnic friction and has recently been rocked by Moslem separatist violence.

Exile groups have said the February riots, which began as a demonstration for Xinjiang independence but turned violent, were sparked by the execution of about 30 Uighurs by the Chinese authorities. Uighur militants say they want to set up their own state of "East Turkestan."
